annotation.speech2: A schematic edge-on view. A green slanted line represents the plane x plus 2 y plus z equals 4. Below it is the point P 0 with coordinates 1, 0, negative 2. A red arrow runs from P 0 perpendicularly to the plane, meeting it at the closest point P with coordinates 11 sixths, 5 thirds, negative 7 sixths; a small square marks the right angle. Two dashed gray segments from P 0 reach the plane at other points and are visibly longer. A blue arrow on the plane shows the normal vector n equals i plus 2 j plus k.
The plane x plus 2 y plus z equals 4, drawn edge-on as a green line.
The point P 0 with coordinates 1, 0, negative 2, lying off the plane.
The shortest segment, drawn in red, from P 0 to the plane. It has length d equals five sixths times the square root of 6 and meets the plane at a right angle.
The closest point P on the plane, with coordinates 11 sixths, 5 thirds, negative 7 sixths.
The normal vector n equals i plus 2 j plus k of the plane, drawn in blue. The shortest segment from P 0 is parallel to it.
A dashed segment from P 0 to another point of the plane, longer than the perpendicular segment.
A second dashed segment from P 0 to another point of the plane, also longer than the perpendicular segment.
